title: Foreign Officials Target AI Companions In Sweeping New Child Safety Push
text:
Photo by Anna Barclay/Getty Images

Officials in the European Union are moving to wall off children from artificial intelligence chatbots and social media platforms.

The European Commission plans to unveil a policy to restrict minors from accessing social media and AI companions before age 15, Politico reported Monday. The EU proposal, called the EU KIDS Act, would restrict Instagram and TikTok and follows Meta’s $17.1 billion August 26 settlement with 47 states over claims it designed its social media platforms to addict children.

The move would establish a tiered approach to age restrictions for children under 15 to access the social media platforms with parental supervision, Politico reported. Children under the age of 13 can only create an account made by their parents, and children between 13 and 15 would be given accounts with contact, screen time, and parental controls.

Once children reach 15 years old, they can create their own accounts on the platforms, according to the outlet.

The proposal will be publicly announced on Thursday, a spokesperson told Politico. (RELATED: OpenAI Doesn’t Want Your Kids Dating Its Chatbot)

JUST IN: 🇪🇺 EU plans to restrict social media and AI chatbot use for children under 15. pic.twitter.com/K6URg7ULR1

“I don’t think these ages are appropriate for use of social media and AI companions. Kids as old as 16 have died by suicide as a result of a perceived emotional ‘relationship’ with AI. These types of age restrictions assume that kids are ready for use of these dangerous products. Even with guardrails, because being on social media, using AI, gaming, streaming TV, etc. takes away from kids doing things in the real world because they are on technology,” Nicole Runyon, a former child psychotherapist and parent coach, told the Daily Caller News Foundation.“So much development gets lost when tech replaces real world acitivity. Like physical movement, tolerating hard things, working through conflict resolution, and learning how to be bored,” Runyon added.

The alogrithm by far is the most dangerous part of the internet. Because it causes children to become addicted, and can give them a scewed perception of the world. I don’t see any governement restrictions on that.

Companies would be required to pay supervisory fees to the European Commission under the proposal, Politico reported.

The European Commission, Meta and TikTok each did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment.

Australia similarly began enforcing social media bans on accounts under 16 in December 2025, according to the New York Times. The country required Instagram, Facebook and Tiktok to incorporate “reasonable steps” to keep children off of their platforms.

In the U.S., Florida bars children under 14 from social media accounts and requires parental consent for 14- and 15-year-olds to use these platforms, according to Florida’s 2024 Online Protections for Minors law.
